studyPlan.task: Read about C++ history and its uses.
Install a C++ compiler (g++) and an editor. Compile Hello World.
Learn statements, semicolons, braces and comments.
Declare and use int, float, double and char variables.
Study primitive types and type sizes with sizeof().
Practice arithmetic, relational and logical operators.
Master cin, cout, and formatted output with iomanip.
Write programs using if, else if, else and switch.
Solve 5 problems using the for loop.
Solve 5 problems using while and do-while loops.
Write functions with parameters and return values.
Create overloaded functions with different parameter types.
Practice 1D array traversal, searching and sorting.
Work with 2D arrays and simple matrix operations.
Use the string class: concatenation, substr, find.
Understand address-of (&) and dereference (*) operators.
Explore pointer arithmetic and pointers to arrays.
Compare references with pointers and pass-by-reference.
Group related data using struct.
Learn the four pillars of OOP with real examples.
Create your first class with constructors.
Build a base and derived class hierarchy.
Use virtual functions and function overriding.
Practice push_back, iteration and sorting a vector.
Use map and set for lookups and uniqueness.
Read and write files with ifstream and ofstream.
Use try, catch and throw to handle runtime errors.
Implement a simple stack and queue using arrays.
Implement bubble sort and binary search from scratch.
Combine everything into one complete console application.

funFacts: C++ was created by Bjarne Stroustrup starting in 1979 at Bell Labs.
C++ was originally called 'C with Classes' before being renamed in 1983.
The '++' in C++ is itself a C increment operator, hinting that C++ is 'one step beyond C'.
C++ is used in game engines like Unreal Engine, and in Chrome, MySQL and Adobe products.
The C++ Standard Template Library (STL) was designed by Alexander Stepanov.
C++11 was such a major update that Stroustrup joked it should feel like a new language.
NASA's Mars rovers run flight software written largely in C++.
C++ allows both low-level memory manipulation and high-level abstraction in the same language.
The first commercial release of C++ was in 1985 with the book 'The C++ Programming Language'.
Bjarne Stroustrup has said 'C makes it easy to shoot yourself in the foot; C++ makes it harder, but when you do it blows your whole leg off.'
Most competitive programming judges (Codeforces, ICPC) use C++ as the default fast language.
The C++ Standard is maintained by ISO, with new versions roughly every 3 years (C++11, 14, 17, 20, 23).
operator overloading in C++ lets you redefine how +, -, == and other symbols behave for your own types.
The keyword 'auto' in modern C++ lets the compiler deduce a variable's type automatically.
Templates in C++ enable generic programming, letting one function work with many data types.

magicTricks.title: Swap Two Numbers Without a Third Variable
magicTricks.teaser: Swap two integer values using arithmetic operations.
magicTricks.reveal: The sum stores both values temporarily. Subtracting recovers the original values in reverse order. For production code, std::swap(a, b) is usually clearer.

magicTricks.title: Find the Larger Number with a Simple Trick
magicTricks.teaser: Use a conditional expression to choose a value in one line.
magicTricks.reveal: The ternary operator checks the condition before ?. If it is true, the first value is selected; otherwise the value after : is selected.

magicTricks.title: Reverse a Number Digit by Digit
magicTricks.teaser: Build a reversed number without converting it to a string.
magicTricks.reveal: n % 10 extracts the last digit. Multiplying rev by 10 shifts its digits left, then the extracted digit is appended.

magicTricks.title: Count Digits with a Tiny Loop
magicTricks.teaser: Count how many digits an integer contains.
magicTricks.reveal: Every integer division by 10 removes one decimal digit. The number of successful divisions is therefore the digit count.

magicTricks.title: Check Even or Odd Instantly
magicTricks.teaser: One operator is enough to test the last binary bit.
magicTricks.reveal: For positive integers, the lowest binary bit is 0 for even values and 1 for odd values. The bitwise AND checks that bit.

magicTricks.title: Swap Using std::swap
magicTricks.teaser: Let the C++ standard library handle swapping safely.
magicTricks.reveal: std::swap is the clean, general-purpose way to exchange values. It avoids arithmetic overflow and works with many C++ types.

magicTricks.title: Make a Constant Value Readable
magicTricks.teaser: Give an important fixed value a clear name.
magicTricks.code:
const double PI = 3.141592653589793;
double area = PI * r * r;
magicTricks.reveal: const prevents accidental modification and makes the meaning of a value obvious. Named constants improve readability and maintenance.

magicTricks.title: Print a Line with a Newline Character
magicTricks.teaser: Use a tiny escape sequence to control output.
magicTricks.reveal: \n inserts a newline in the output stream. It is useful when you want precise control over where the next output begins.
